label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
**Lee – have a read before you say no to the dumper**

I reckon it’s worth us going halves on a secondhand tracked dumper instead of hiring one every time. I know you’ll want the numbers, so here they are.

**What hire’s costing us**

We’ve hired the dumper for 14 days this year from the place in Sittingbourne. At £85 a day, plus £30 delivery each time, we’ve spent roughly **£1,600 all in**.

There’s one for sale in Faversham: a **2019 500kg tracked dumper, £1,650 ono**. The seller says it had new tracks fitted last spring. Halves at the full asking price is **£825 each**, and we can try knocking him down once we’ve looked it over.

At this year’s level of use, it would pay for itself in about a year. Even if we only used it half as much, it’s roughly two years. That’s before servicing and repairs, so I’m not pretending it’ll cost nothing to run.

**Why it makes sense**

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked in for spring, so it won’t be sitting about doing nothing.

It also saves us relying on the hire place. In September they didn’t have one available and we ended up barrowing six ton of muck at Hernhill. That added two days and your back was gone for a week. Another time the delivery driver didn’t turn up until 11, so we lost half the morning before we’d even started.

Having our own means it’s there when we need it. It can live under cover in my lean-to at the yard, so storage’s sorted.

**Costs and if it goes wrong**

Servicing and normal running costs would be **50/50**. Whoever breaks it pays to put it right. Simple as that.

If it turns out not to suit us, we sell it on and split what we get. These seem to hold their value, so I don’t think we’re taking a massive punt.

After 15 years of working together, I reckon we can make this work without any messing about.

Come and look at it with me **this Saturday** before somebody else has it. If it’s rough, we walk away. If it’s as described, I think it’s a sound buy.
